newsitem.title: JAPAN: LME officials say to meet MITI officials in Japan.
newsitem.headline: LME officials say to meet MITI officials in Japan.

text.p: Top officials from the London Metal Exchange said they would meet Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) officials during their visit to Japan this week, although they said it would be a routine courtesy call.
"We'll probably be talking about warehousing and TOCOM (Tokyo Commodity Exchange) and things like that," LME chief executive David King told a Tokyo news conference on Tuesday.
LME officials at the news conference repeatedly stressed that their visit was not prompted by the Sumitomo Corp copper trading scandal.
The LME officials are visiting Japan and Australia to meet government officials and users.
LME chairman Raj Bagri said contact with Sumitomo officials on this trip would probably be limited to shaking hands at a luncheon on Tuesday.

Sumitomo rocked the world's copper markets in mid-June when it announced massive copper trading losses that it now estimates at $2.6 billion. British and U.S. regulators are currently investigating the affair.
"We continue to have a dialogue with regulatory authorities around the world," King said. "And we have an ongoing dialogue with Sumitomo Corp."
